item.title: Banking and Credit Research Roundtable
item.description: Experts Nils, Sarah, and Rajesh join host Paul to discuss three recent academic papers on credit surfaces, fintech borrower behavior, and the capitalization of private credit funds. The roundtable explores how empirical data is reshaping our understanding of risk, search costs, and financial stability in the modern economy.
item.itunes:author: Paul

item.title: AI: Entrepreneurial Boom or Bust?
item.description: This episode explores the impact of AI on business formation, discussing whether generative AI is democratizing entrepreneurship or creating a digital divide. Experts debate current trends in corporate AI adoption, highlighting the gap between employee enthusiasm and executive skepticism.
item.itunes:author: Paul

item.title: Banks and Private Credit Risks
item.description: This episode examines the systemic risks arising from banks shifting their direct corporate lending to indirect exposures through private credit funds. The panel debates whether valuation smoothing in private markets acts as a stabilizing feature or a dangerous illusion that hides credit deterioration.
item.itunes:author: Paul

item.title: The Evolution of Modern Banking
item.description: This episode explores how banks act as crucial information processors through delegated monitoring and soft information. The discussion compares traditional relationship banking with modern algorithmic fintech solutions, highlighting the enduring value of human nuance during crises.
item.itunes:author: Paul
